blockingFindings.title: Command behavior and validation are only checked by string presence

It does not exercise add, update, show, search, list, publish, or ideas behavior, and it does not test user-facing argument or option validation at the plugin command entry point.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Add spec-local executable command-entry tests for each workflow subcommand, including representative valid input and invalid argument/option cases from the validation contract.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: R2's central acceptance requirement can pass with a stub file or comments, so the coverage artifact claims coverage that the actual test does not provide.

blockingFindings.title: Plugin-owned shared services are not proven to be used
blockingFindings.issue: The R3 test only checks that service filenames exist and that hooks do not shell out to the workflow CLI. Empty service files or duplicated command/hook implementations would pass.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Add tests that verify workflow commands and hooks call the plugin-owned board, publish, issue-start, and ideas services through shared service APIs, preferably with stubs/spies at the service boundary.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: R3 requires plugin-owned services shared by commands and hooks for specific behavior; filename existence does not exercise production behavior or sharing.

blockingFindings.title: Flow hook lifecycle contract is not exercised
blockingFindings.issue: The R4 test searches hook source for prepare/finalize strings and issue-log related words, but does not verify that core runs prepare.post after writing flow state with hook snapshot, spec path, runId, and linked issue, nor that finalize-cleanup.post receives durable spec/issue-log/artifact paths. It also does not verify non-fatal handling for board config, gh, or AI refinement failures.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Add integration-style tests for the generic flow lifecycle invoking prepare.post and finalize-cleanup.post hooks with asserted context fields and simulated business failures that produce warnings, issue-log entries, or follow-ups without failing the main command.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: The required core/plugin lifecycle behavior is critical and currently untested; the existing regex test would pass without the hook contract working.

blockingFindings.title: AI provider/profile override behavior is not covered

blockingFindings.title: Removed public subcommands can still pass the test

blockingFindings.whyBlocking: R9 explicitly requires removal without compatibility aliases; the current static pattern can miss the prohibited API surface.

blockingFindings.title: Installability and smoke verification are not tested

requirements.desc: Prepare the external workflow plugin repository under the active flow worktree and perform plugin-side implementation and verification from that in-boundary location.

The workflow plugin must own the `senti workflow` top-level command and existing add, update, show, search, list, publish, and ideas behavior without importing core src/workflow modules or relying on a bundled compatibility copy. Each user-facing argument and option must be validated at the plugin command entry point according to the validation contract in clarifications.
The workflow plugin must provide plugin-owned services shared by commands and hooks for board item operations, issue publishing, issue-start behavior, and board idea candidate extraction.

The workflow plugin must provide prepare.post and finalize-cleanup.post hooks for flow integration. Generic core lifecycle must run prepare.post with the newly written flow state including hook snapshot, spec path, runId, and linked issue, and must run finalize-cleanup.post while a durable spec/issue-log/artifact path is available. Hook business failures such as board config missing, gh failure, or AI refinement failure must produce warnings, issue-log entries, or follow-ups without failing the main flow command.

Workflow plugin AI call sites for publish, idea candidate classification, similarity, and composition must resolve provider/profile overrides from plugin.config.workflow.agent.<name> and otherwise use a workflow-neutral public plugin agent API/context that exposes generic agent resolve/call capability and needed root config values such as lang.

Core must remove workflow-owned runtime implementation and bundled workflow compatibility artifacts, including src/workflow and src/official-plugins/senti-workflow-plugin, after their behavior is available from the external plugin.

Core must remove workflow-specific config schema/defaults/migration, workflow.publish default agent profile entries, official workflow bootstrap special-cases, and workflow-specific help/locale entries, while preserving generic plugin and preset behavior.

Core flow prompt and skill source must stop hardcoding workflow board integration, issue-start, issue-log-import, workflow add, or workflow.flowIntegration instructions. Equivalent behavior must be provided through workflow plugin hooks and plugin-owned follow-up text.

Public workflow subcommands issue-start and issue-log-import must be removed without compatibility aliases. The migration plan must replace issue-start with prepare.post hook behavior and issue-log-import with the ideas command and updated skill/help guidance.

Core tests must not contain workflow-specific feature fixtures or expectations after migration. Core may keep generic plugin contract tests using non-workflow sample plugins, and workflow behavior tests must live with the workflow plugin.
The migrated workflow plugin must be installable/enabled for this repository from the external plugin repository and provide a smoke-verifiable `senti workflow` command plus flow hook behavior.

If migration changes src/skills, src/presets, source templates, or deployed skill artifacts, the implementation must run senti upgrade and include evidence that generated artifacts match source changes.

advisoryFindings.title: R7 locale/help cleanup scan is narrow
advisoryFindings.improvement: Broaden the R7 assertion to scan all relevant core help and locale files for workflow-specific command/help text, not only two exact strings in ui.json.
advisoryFindings.whyNonBlocking: The existing test does cover major config/bootstrap/default removal and checks known locale strings, but broader scanning would reduce the chance of missed workflow wording.
